newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line hopes for EU approval of Channel scheme.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line hopes for EU approval of Channel scheme.

text.p: Swedish ferry operator Stena Line said on Wednesday that the European Union (EU) had issued a "letter of serious doubts" about its planned joint venture with British P&O's on the English Channel routes as expected.
But Stena Line and P&O, the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company, hope to get an EU nod for the project through a "letter of comfort" at the start of July, the group said in a statement.
The "letter of serious doubts" confirmed the EU Commission has accepted that the new company, called P&O Stena Line, would meet strong competition on the freight market, Stena Line said.
"On the passenger side, the EU Commission said it wanted complementary discussions about fears for a possible future duopoly consisting of the Eurotunnel and P&O Stena Line," Stena Line said.
The Commission also underlined that it wanted operations in the merged company to be separated from operations in the parent companies, Stena Line said.
"The facts for creating a common company with P&O are overwhelming," Stena Line chief executive Bo Lerenius said.
"The message from the EU is in line with our expectations and we will now quickly start complementary discussions with the Commission to sort out remaining questions."
